Dear Partners,

The quarter delivered the kind of macro noise that keeps allocators busy and strategists employed. The central bank held its policy rate at 4.75%, inflation continued its glide path to 2.7%, and credit markets stayed constructive, with high-yield spreads at 380bps — hardly a backdrop suggesting stress. Public equities, meanwhile, staged a vigorous rally, up +9.0% for the quarter. Investors could be forgiven for asking why our own reported figures did not keep pace. We would rather answer that question directly than let it linger.

Our flagship reported +0.5% for the quarter, bringing year-to-date performance to +1.0% and since-inception returns to +28.0%. The NAV index closed at 101.0. We recognize the gap between that print and the public market's +9.0% surge is wider than we would like to see in any single quarter, and it warrants comment rather than silence.

Listed comparables have rerated sharply in recent weeks, and the public rally has left private marks looking comparatively muted. We would frame it differently: private valuations are constructed on a cadence and methodology built for durability, not for chasing every intraday swing in public indices. What the market is pricing as instantaneous re-rating, our process captures with appropriate lag and discipline. This is not a concession that our marks are behind reality — it is a function of temporal dislocation between how public and private assets are marked, and we would encourage limited partners to view the coming quarters, not this one in isolation, as the fairer test.

Underneath the headline, portfolio operations remain a source of quiet confidence. Working alongside our operating partners, our companies continue to execute on margin initiatives and pricing discipline that don't always show up in a single quarter's mark but compound meaningfully over a hold period. Diligence work alongside our internal team continues to validate underwriting theses across the portfolio, even where reported figures lag the story.

Looking ahead, we remain constructive, though prudently so. Tighter spreads and a stabilizing rate environment are supportive conditions for refinancing activity across the vintage, and we are engaged with external partners on structuring options where prudent. That said, we would be doing our investors a disservice if we did not flag that leverage taken on at earlier-vintage entry multiples remains a variable worth watching closely.
